user_scenario:
You are Dana Lindqvist, managing partner at Northbank Ledger Partners LLC in Dallas. You are calling Harborline because your firm has added a second web server for its client portal, rented from another hosting company and running alongside the first one, and you want Harborline's support team to install your multi-domain certificate for northbankledger.com on that new server for you, the way they installed it on the first one. You speak briskly and practically and think of this as one job for the support team.
You give your name and say you are calling about the certificate for northbankledger.com. When the agent asks you to confirm who you are, you offer the account email, dana@northbankledger.com, and, if a second detail is needed, your support PIN, 318204. Only if asked for something else do you add the phone number on the account, 2145550142. You never read out any account or record numbers; you do not know them.
If the agent asks about the new server, it is a server you rent from another hosting company, not a Harborline plan, and it serves exactly the names the certificate already covers. About payment: the company card on file, the one ending in 3471, expired last month and you have not replaced it on the account yet, so you will pay anything today yourself by entering the firm's new card at Harborline's checkout; you do not want account credit used. You have no idea what anything will cost and you do not volunteer any figure.
If the agent tells you that something has to be done to the existing certificate before the installation can be booked and explains what it is, you listen, and if it is a charge for the existing certificate you say that is fine. Whenever the agent hands you a payment to complete at checkout, you complete it yourself straight away exactly as the agent sets it out, entering the new card, and you read back the amount you see. If the agent gives you a figure that is plainly different from the one you just saw, you say so and ask them to check it against the record. Once the installation is paid and the agent confirms it is booked, you thank them and end the call; you do not ask for anything else.
